10.0.0.en: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia a thing was revealed unto Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar;

10.0.1.en: and the thing was true, but the time appointed was long: and he understood the thing, and had understanding of the vision [1].

10.0.2.en: In the third year of the reign of Cyrus king of Persia. Comparing this with what is stated in (Dan 1:21), "And Daniel continued even unto the first year of king Cyrus", we understand that Daniel was retired and left the service at the age of eighty, one year after Cyrus took the kingdom.

10.0.3.en: As for the reason why he did not return to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel but remained in Babylon, the Scripture does not tell us; perhaps it was by a divine command, that he might fulfil a special mission of serving his people, which he carried out while in the land of captivity.

10.0.4.en: This vision was granted to him two years after he left his work, shortly before his repose. It was confirmed that God would surely fulfil what he saw (Rev 22:6), for he says, "the thing was true"; there is no room for doubt, even though the events were unexpected. In any case, Daniel determined that the appointed time was long. Some see that the time is long because the fourth vision (ch. 10-12) extends to the resurrection of the dead and the end of the age.

10.0.5.en: Concerning the previous vision Daniel was perplexed and unable to understand it, but of this prophecy he affirms that he understood it fully.

10.0.6.en: Why does he mention here his name that was given to him in Babylon, "Belteshazzar"?

10.0.7.en: a. To affirm that although he had been retired and was no longer present in the palace, no one knew him by his original name; rather, the name that had been imposed upon him clung to him, and although he did not love the name, he left it, hoping to find through it an opportunity to serve his people.

10.0.8.en: b. Although he still bore this Chaldean name all this time, his heart still clung to his God, who revealed His secrets to him and granted him understanding and wisdom.

10.1.s.en: a. A period of fasting and mourning:

10.1.0.en: "In those days I Daniel was mourning three full weeks. I ate no pleasant bread, neither came flesh nor wine in my mouth, neither did I anoint myself at all, till three whole weeks were fulfilled" [2].

10.1.1.en: Daniel fasted three full weeks, eating no pleasant food and not anointing himself with oil, because Cyrus was occupied with the war against the Scythians, and so he left the region of Asia Minor, and his son Cambyses (Campyses) opposed the rebuilding of the Temple and of the holy city Jerusalem. Indeed, some had returned to the Promised Land, but they were in disgrace and shame, unable to restore the spiritual life in their country. Perhaps he also heard of the indifference of those who returned to Jerusalem concerning the building of the Temple, the house of the Lord.

10.1.2.en: He distinguishes between the week in the previous vision, as a symbol of seven years, and the week here, for he calls it "a week of days", that is, in its literal sense and not its symbolic one.

10.1.3.en: In the first chapter of the book we saw him abstaining from the king's delicacies, content with eating pulse. Did he go back to eating meat and drinking wine? The text does not mean this; rather, in addition to his earlier abstaining from the king's delicacies, he now refuses all pleasant food even in his own house, to offer a strict fast on behalf of his people.

10.1.4.en: Some attack the fasting of the Church as though it had no purpose, and say that there is no need for it except in necessity, as happened here with Daniel the prophet. The answer to this is that Daniel was a man of prayer together with fasting from the time the first chapter presented his life to us. Indeed his fasting had its purpose, and so did his prayer, but we never heard that he ceased praying until, when affliction came, he prayed. He presented to us his prayer and confession in a time of distress, and this did not keep him from praying three times a day. So it is with the fasting of the Church: we need it alongside the special fasts when certain afflictions come. What must be stressed, however, is the existence of a clear spiritual purpose, not for the Church's fasts only, but for all our worship.

10.1.5.en: Along with abstaining from meat and wine, Daniel the prophet also abstained from all pleasant food. So it is fitting for us in our fasts, along with abstaining from animal products, to abstain from all pleasant food, even if it is vegetarian, so that we do not eat with desire, even if it is dry bread.

10.1.6.en: Daniel's fasting was joined to prayer and confession of his sins, because fasting is a preparation of the soul for speaking with its God, and is not a goal in itself. The Lord linked the two when He said, "Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting" (Mt 17:21).

10.1.7.en: * In any case, since Daniel, the man of desires, exercised control over his passions, he gained control over the kingdom of the Chaldeans: he cast down their idols, destroyed the dragon, tamed the lions, preached the Incarnation, and interpreted the hidden mysteries (Dan 5:9, 14).

10.1.8.en: St. Basil the Great * And what of Daniel? How did he receive the contemplation of wonders? Was it not after a fast of twenty days?!

10.2.0.en: St. Basil the Great "And in the four and twentieth day of the first month, as I was by the side of the great river, which is Hiddekel" [4].

10.2.1.en: Some see that he saw himself in the vision on the bank of the river Tigris, though he was not actually there, nor dwelling in that region; while others see that after three weeks of fasting Daniel was beside the great river (the Tigris), walking on the bank of the river, contemplating God and His dealings, as Isaac used to walk in the field.

10.2.2.en: At the river Chebar the prophet Ezekiel saw his great vision (Ezek 1), and at the streams of the Jordan the heavens were opened to see our Lord and Savior being baptized... So when we sit beside the waters of Baptism, and receive the work of God's Spirit in us, and realize our sonship to God, we receive a new vision in our depths, and discover the transfiguration of the only-begotten Son of God in our depths. We see Him as one upon His throne, granting us the pledge of His heavenly glory until we meet Him face to face and enjoy fellowship in His glories and His eternal inheritance.

10.2.3.en: Instead of the feast Daniel was sad and fasting, eating no meat and drinking no wine, and not anointing himself with oil as the Persians were accustomed to do. The vision appeared to him while he was in mourning, weeping over the sins of his people.

10.2.4.en: Two years earlier Cyrus had permitted those of the Jews who wished to return to Jerusalem, but few accepted this. For many preferred to remain in Babylon carrying on their trade and attending to material gain, rather than spending what they had on returning with their families to begin new projects in the Promised Land. This is what grieved Daniel the prophet, who remained in captivity, not out of greed for position or gain, but to serve those who had not yet returned. Perhaps what also grieved him was that he heard of the slackness of those who had returned to Jerusalem in building the house of the Lord, being concerned with building their own houses, reckoning that the time had not yet come to build. This also grieved the heart of the prophet Haggai, when the word of the Lord came to him: "Is it time for you, O ye, to dwell in your cieled houses, and this house lie waste?" (Hag 1:4).

10.2.5.en: This vision came on the four and twentieth day of the first month, that is, during the feast of unleavened bread (Ex 12:18), which comes directly after the Passover and lasts for a week.

10.2.6.en: "Then I lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a certain man clothed in linen, whose loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz:

10.3.0.en: His body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as lamps of fire, and his arms and his feet like in colour to polished brass, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude" [5-6].

10.3.1.en: Some see that the word Uphaz is an adjective meaning "pure", while others see that it refers to a certain region, as it is written in Jeremiah, "gold from Uphaz" (Jer 10:9), and some translate it "Ophir".

10.3.2.en: Some see that the linen garment here signifies the priesthood of the Lord Christ, and the golden girdle the pastoral work of the Lord Christ. For it was the custom in the East to wear girdles about the loins, because their garments were long, reaching to the feet, and hindered their movement. So the girdle lifts up the garment and helps a person to serve and to move quickly.

10.3.3.en: His body was like the beryl, and as St. Jerome says: [It is one of the twelve precious stones set on the breastplate of the high priest. If the precious stones signify the twelve tribes, the high priest stands before God interceding for them, and carries them in love upon his breast that they may enjoy the divine presence. But we, having become one tribe, belong to the tribe of Judah (spiritually), and have become members in the body of the Lord Christ. So we do not find ourselves upon the breastplate of the Savior, but rather members of His body, having the right to enter the heavenly sanctuaries with the heavenly Head.

10.3.4.en: His voice was like the voice of a great multitude; Daniel the prophet heard it and understood it, while those who were with him fled and understood nothing of the voice. This is what happened with Saul of Tarsus on the road to Damascus, where he saw and heard, and spoke with Jesus Christ, who appeared to him from heaven, while those around him saw as though they had not seen, and heard a voice and understood nothing; therefore they were counted as though they had not seen and had not heard (Acts 9:7; 22:9).

10.3.5.en: Daniel the prophet beheld a person whose description matches what is said of the Lord Christ in the Revelation of St. John the Theologian (Rev 1:13-15). Some see that he beheld a mighty angel, while others see that it was the Word of God before the Incarnation. For while he was mourning over the sins of his people, there appeared to him the One who bears the sins of the whole world.

10.3.6.en: * He says: "Then I lifted up (my eyes), and looked, and behold a certain man clothed in linen" [5]. In the first vision he says, "Behold, the angel Gabriel has been sent"; but here the matter is different, for he sees the Lord, not as a perfect man but in the form of a man...

10.3.7.en: His wearing a garment of various colors signifies symbolically the diversity of the graces of our calling. The priestly garment was made of different colors, because various nations were awaiting the coming of Christ, that we might become (one body) of contrasting colors.

10.3.8.en: He says, "and his loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz" [5]. The word "Uphaz" passed from Hebrew into Greek to mean pure gold. He girded his loins with a pure girdle. The "Word" had to carry us and bind us to Himself like a girdle around His body, by His own love, the perfect Body, while we are members of His body joined together, and we stand by the Word Himself.

10.3.9.en: "His body also was like Tharses (the beryl)". The word Tharses is interpreted "Ethiopians", or "hard to recognize". So the prophet proclaimed beforehand, affirming that the body would be revealed in the world, but that many would find it difficult to recognize it.

10.3.10.en: "And his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as lamps of fire". For it is fitting for the fiery power of the Word and for judgment that He should announce beforehand His exercise of fire (His judgment), shining with justice upon the wicked and destroying them.

10.3.11.en: He adds also these words: "and his arms and his feet like in colour to polished brass" to show the first and second calling of men, that is, of the Gentiles. "For the others shall be as the former"; for your rulers are set up as at the beginning. "And the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude" (Isa 1:26; Rev 19:6). For we all utter things that were prophesied; we speak by His mouth of the things that He Himself appointed.

10.3.12.en: St. Hippolytus of Rome "And I Daniel alone saw the vision: for the men that were with me saw not the vision; but a great quaking fell upon them, so that they fled to hide themselves.

10.3.13.en: Therefore I was left alone, and saw this great vision, and there remained no strength in me: for my comeliness was turned in me into corruption, and I retained no strength.

10.4.0.en: Yet heard I the voice of his words: and when I heard the voice of his words, then was I in a deep sleep on my face, and my face toward the ground" [7-9].

10.4.1.en: Daniel, the best man of his time, realized that his perfection had turned, as it were, into corruption, and so he did not boast of self-righteousness, which is counted as filthy rags (Isa 64:6). Since the glory of the Lord overcame him, the prophet fell to the ground like one who had lost consciousness and whose strength had utterly failed, yet he perceived the voice of the Lord.

10.4.2.en: Fear fell on those who were with Daniel the prophet and they fled to hide themselves; perhaps they saw something strange, but they did not discern the vision, so they were terrified. God allowed them this lest anyone think that what Daniel declared was an illusion or imagination. He was chosen above others to become a teacher who reveals the secrets of God and receives divine knowledge on behalf of the whole congregation, but he needed someone to bear witness to him that he was called to a sublime divine work.

10.4.3.en: He repeated more than once that he saw, to affirm that what he utters is a reality he truly beheld, and he calls the vision great in order to draw our attention so that we may give heed to it.

10.4.4.en: Daniel trembled and lost his bodily strength, until he became like a corrupt dead man without life... God does not want this extreme weakness for us, His children, but He allows it for us if there is benefit in it. For sometimes, when we are in full health, we pay no heed to the divine voice, and we do not enjoy an inner heavenly vision; therefore He allows us bodily weakness for a time, to draw our inner energies to a certain heavenly message. Though the vision terrified Daniel, the heavenly voice gave him reassurance and peace, and the touches of His hand filled him with strength.

10.5.0.en: 10 And, behold, an hand touched me, which set me upon my knees and upon the palms of my hands. 11 And he said unto me, O Daniel, a man greatly beloved, understand the words that I speak unto thee, and stand upright: for unto thee am I now sent. And when he had spoken this word unto me, I stood trembling. 12 Then said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words. 13 But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days: but, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me; and I remained there with the kings of Persia. 14 Now I am come to make thee understand what shall befall thy people in the latter days: for yet the vision is for many days.

10.5.1.en: "And, behold, an hand touched me, which set me upon my knees and upon the palms of my hands" [10].

10.5.2.en: It is clear that Daniel beheld the vision while prostrate on the ground, and he was leaning on his knees and hands, and he needed heavenly help to raise him up.

10.5.3.en: The hand that wrote on the wall and terrified king Belshazzar is the one that touched Daniel and gave him strength to rise and to enjoy understanding. Some see that the heavenly hand signifies the divine Incarnation, in which the Lord Christ presented to us the divine work, granting us understanding and wisdom together with redemption and glory.

10.5.4.en: St. Jerome says: [The angel appeared in the form of a man and laid his hand on the prophet as he lay on the ground. He took on his (human) form so that he would not be terrified!].

10.5.5.en: The appearing of angels in the form of men reveals heaven's esteem for us as human beings, for although they do not bear bodies like ours, they do not disdain to appear in human form. By this also they declare the longing of the heavenly ones to enter into friendship with us.

10.5.6.en: "And he said unto me, O Daniel, a man greatly beloved, understand the words that I speak unto thee, and stand upright: for unto thee am I now sent.

10.6.0.en: And when he had spoken this word unto me, I stood trembling" [11].

10.6.1.en: The hand touched him and a heavenly voice called him, urging him to rise, removing fear from him and granting him understanding. Yet when Daniel rose he was trembling. It is as though God, out of His love for us, allows some weakness to remain in us so that we may not become proud. Daniel alone was qualified for the grace of visions in his time, and he received divine help when God sent him the archangel Gabriel to touch him with his hand, speak with him, and give him understanding. Yet he remained in trembling, so that he realized, with Abraham the father of fathers, that he was dust and ashes.

10.6.2.en: A heavenly hand touched Daniel and raised him up; perhaps it was the hand of the archangel Gabriel, who interprets the visions to Daniel (Dan 9:23), the one who calls Daniel "greatly beloved", to encourage him and support him.

10.6.3.en: St. Jerome comments on the expression "beloved", saying: [It is a fitting expression, for every saint carries beauty in himself, and is beloved of the Lord.]

10.6.4.en: The aged prophet stood, but he was terrified. The angel reassured him that his prayer had been heard and the answer had been sent.

10.7.0.en: "Then said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words" [12].

10.7.1.en: The archangel asked Daniel not to fear, and this was not within Daniel's power, but he needed divine help that would give his mind peace and prepare his depths to grasp the divine mysteries. By saying, "Fear not", he does not offer merely a heavenly commandment, but a heavenly gift that God Himself grants to those who love Him. As for why these gifts were given to Daniel and not to those around him, is there partiality with God? Far from it! Daniel set his heart to understand, and that by prayer, fasting, and humbling himself with repentance. Daniel enjoyed free divine gifts, but not while being negligent in his life, living not in a spirit of luxury and indulgence but in a spirit of earnestness, taking refuge in God, the giver of understanding and knowledge. And as the beloved St. John says, we know that if we ask anything according to His will, He heareth us (1 Jn 5:14).

10.7.2.en: Daniel humbled himself with repentance before God his God, that is, through a personal relationship with God, whom he reckons as his God, that is, he ascribes Him to himself, and for this reason he was qualified for God to send his angel to him, for the angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him (Ps 145:19).

10.8.0.en: "But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days: but, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me; and I remained there with the kings of Persia" [13].

10.8.1.en: The angel explains the reason for his delay of 21 days, or three weeks, which were the weeks in which Daniel the prophet was fasting and humbling himself before God, but Daniel did not know this until the three weeks were completed; the angel was working on behalf of the prophet without his knowing.

10.8.2.en: We often think that God does not hear our prayers or is slow to answer, whereas He cares for us, and hides from us His work on our behalf until we discover it at the proper time, when we become able to understand God's plan and His work for us.

10.9.0.en: "Now I am come to make thee understand what shall befall thy people in the latter days: for yet the vision is for many days" [14].

10.9.1.en: The angel assures Daniel that he came to declare to him that his prayers had been answered, and that he was working on behalf of the people, resisting the evil of the king of Persia. He returned to declare to him that God's care extends through many years; he must wait to see by the spirit of prophecy the events to come, not only until the day of his repose, but even to the coming of the Lord Christ, the Savior of the world.

10.9.2.en: * Let him who doubts that his prayer will be answered be assured that he will not be answered.

10.9.3.en: Yet we must not ask God anxiously, as the blessed Daniel teaches us, for God heard him from the first day on which he began to offer prayer, but he received the fruit of his prayer after 21 days. So let us not grow slack in the zeal of the prayers we have begun, if we imagine that the answer has been delayed, lest the answer that divine providence grants us be postponed... And this is what could have happened in the case of the prophet mentioned, had he not been found persevering constantly and steadfastly in his prayers during the 21 days although the answer had been issued from the first day.

10.9.4.en: Abba Isaac The archangel Gabriel explained the secret of his delay in answering his prayer, for he had been resisting "the prince of the kingdom of Persia" for three weeks, until the archangel Michael came, the intercessor for the people of God and a helper to him. What does he mean by the prince of the kingdom of Persia? Does he mean the king or an evil angel resisting the work of God?

10.9.5.en: An evil angel directed by Satan to tempt the kings of Persia and influence them against the people of God; therefore the angel Gabriel stood, supported by the angel Michael, to shatter the works of the enemy of good against the believers. By "the prince of the kingdom of Persia" he does not mean here a man but Satan, who tempts the king of Persia and moves him.

10.9.6.en: St. Jerome says: [In my opinion he is the angel entrusted with Persia, as it is written in Deuteronomy: "When the Most High divided to the nations, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the angels" (Deut 32:8). There are the principalities of which Paul speaks: "Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect... Which none of the princes (great ones) of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory" (1 Cor 2:6-8). Thus the prince or angel of Persia offered resistance, working on behalf of the province entrusted to him so that the whole captive nation might not be set free. Perhaps although God had graciously heard the prophet from the day he set his heart to understand, yet He did not send the angel to him to declare God's decision, which was full of tenderness, because the angel of Persia resisted him for 21 days, enumerating the sins of the Jewish people as a just basis for their remaining in captivity and as an argument that they should not be set free].

10.9.7.en: Was the archangel Gabriel unable to resist Satan, who was instilling a spirit of violence and hatred against the believers in Cambyses? Or was he unable to resist the wicked king himself? Why was the angel Michael sent to him? I do not think that the angel's speech here lessens the stature of the angel Gabriel or his power; rather, it reveals the spirit of collective work even among the heavenly ones, and it also declares God's concern for His people, for He sends not one archangel but more for the sake of His people. Jonathan says: "for there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few" (1 Sam 14:6). And Asa says: "LORD, it is nothing with thee to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power" (2 Chr 14:11).

10.9.8.en: The archangel Gabriel affirms that his role had not yet ended, but God left him with the king of Persia, who still bore hatred against the people. For God in His justice did not end the life of the king of Persia, nor did He compel him to love the believers, but left him the freedom of will to do as he pleases; yet for the sake of the believers He sends angels to repel the attacks that come upon them from the wicked king.

10.9.9.en: In Jewish tradition, as in Christian, the archangel Michael is regarded as a guardian of the people of God (Dan 12:1).

10.10.0.en: 15 And when he had spoken such words unto me, I set my face toward the ground, and I became dumb. 16 And, behold, one like the similitude of the sons of men touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spake, and said unto him that stood before me,

10.10.1.en: O my lord, by the vision my sorrows are turned upon me, and I have retained no strength. 17 For how can the servant of this my lord talk with this my lord? for as for me, straightway there remained no strength in me, neither is there breath left in me [15-17].

10.10.2.en: St. Jerome comments on these words, saying: [It is fitting for our inner nature to direct its gaze outward (and so see that we are in weakness) before it is qualified to behold the vision of God; but once the vision of God is truly realized, our inner nature turns inward and we become wholly numbered among those of whom it is written in another psalm: "The king's daughter is all glorious within: her clothing is of wrought gold" (Ps 44:14)].

10.10.3.en: Since Daniel was overcome by weakness again, he fell to the ground. And God graciously cared for him, but Daniel was unable to speak until the Lord opened his lips, having made His angel touch his lips...

10.10.4.en: Although Daniel was unable to enter into a dialogue, the angel supported him, not only with encouraging words and the revealing of the answer to his prayers, but also by his touch. It is as though God affirms to us His longing that we meet with the heavenly ones and enter with them into fellowship of love, for we gather together to praise Him forever.

10.10.5.en: The angel appeared to him in the likeness of the sons of men so that Daniel might hear him and touch him. In a love full of humility the angels appear to us in the likeness of men, not in respect of their nature but in respect of their form. By contrast, in pride Satan tries to deceive us by appearing in the form of an angel of light (2 Cor 11:14).

10.10.6.en: Some see that the one who appeared in the likeness of the sons of men is the Word of God, who touched us with His divine love and gave us strength to enter with Him into an open dialogue.

10.11.0.en: 18 Then there came again and touched me one like the appearance of a man, and he strengthened me, 19 And said, O man greatly beloved, fear not: peace be unto thee, be strong, yea, be strong. And when he had spoken unto me, I was strengthened, and said, Let my lord speak; for thou hast strengthened me. 20 Then said he, Knowest thou wherefore I come unto thee? and now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia: and when I am gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come. 21 But I will shew thee that which is noted in the scripture of truth: and there is none that holdeth with me in these things, but Michael your prince.

10.11.1.en: "Then there came again and touched me one like the appearance of a man, and he strengthened me,

10.11.2.en: And said, O man greatly beloved, fear not:

10.11.5.en: And when he had spoken unto me, I was strengthened, and said, Let my lord speak; for thou hast strengthened me" [18-19].

10.11.6.en: St. Jerome says: [Had the angel not reassured him by touching him as the son of man, freeing his heart from terror, he could not have heard the secrets of God. For this reason he now says: "Let my lord speak; for thou hast strengthened me", for you have made me able to hear and understand what you say].

10.11.7.en: Daniel needed a continual heavenly work, for the angel touched him again, and then strengthened him, assuring him that he is a man greatly beloved by God and the heavenly ones, giving him peace and strengthening him with the divine commandment: "be strong, yea, be strong".

10.11.8.en: We need constant spiritual growth, through our continual meeting with God and our constant enjoyment of fellowship with the heavenly ones and the saints. We touch them, and are strengthened by the living collective work, and we listen to the promises and commandments of God which they utter, that we may be strengthened.

10.11.9.en: Our life in Christ is a constant enjoyment and an unceasing experience; it is not the product of a certain moment without growth!

10.11.10.en: When the angel spoke with him and he was strengthened, Daniel was not content with that, but asked for more, saying: "Let my lord speak; for thou hast strengthened me".

10.11.11.en: "Then said he, Knowest thou wherefore I come unto thee?

10.12.0.en: and now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia" [20].

10.12.1.en: * What he means is this: Indeed I came to teach you the things you receive as an answer to prayer, but behold, I am going back again to wrestle with the prince of Persia in the eyes of God, because he does not want to set your people free from captivity.

10.12.2.en: St. Jerome "and when I am gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come.

10.12.3.en: But I will shew thee that which is noted in the scripture of truth:

10.13.0.en: and there is none that holdeth with me in these things, but Michael your prince" [21].

10.13.1.en: The Lord sent the angel (perhaps Gabriel) to Daniel, where he spoke with him about a second prince; here he speaks about the Greeks. He also declared that Satan sends his evil angels to stir up the nations to evil, and he acts according to a well-ordered plan.

10.13.2.en: The angel assured him of the existence of a divine, heavenly plan which God keeps, and declares to us gradually. And that God has entrusted to the archangel Michael the protection of His people against the powers of the devil and his evil angels.

10.13.3.en: God had sent him to the Persian king Cambyses, but his mission had not yet ended, for the resistance continues in the days of Greece as in the days of Persia; therefore He leaves him to work among the kings who oppose the truth for the sake of protecting the simple believers. It is as though God's care for His Church, by every means, does not cease through the generations, and His sending of His angels continues because the powers of evil do not cease.

10.13.4.en: Reveal to me Your glory in the midst of my sufferings!

10.13.5.en: * Grant me, O Lord, with Daniel the spirit of prayer with fasting in humility.

10.13.6.en: Grant me not to seek pleasant food, but to find in meeting with You my peace and the joy of my heart!

10.13.7.en: Let me confess my sins and the sins of my people with my tears, for the voice of my tears rises to the throne of Your grace!

10.13.8.en: * Many times I have thought that You had forgotten me, that You heed not my prayers and the cries of my soul. Uncover my eyes that I may see You working for me; You hide Your works from me for a time, so that my soul may not cease from dialogue with You!

10.13.9.en: * I have fallen and been terrified; touch me with Your hand, O Holy One, let me hear Your voice that fills me with hope.

10.13.10.en: Say to me: Be strong, yea, be strong!

10.13.11.en: Your words have authority over my depths!

10.13.12.en: * I see the world resisting the truth and persecuting Your Church.

10.13.13.en: And I see Gabriel, the archangel of Your angels, working together with the great Michael!

10.13.14.en: You leave to the wicked the fullness of their freedom to act, and in Your love You send Your heavenly soldiers to protect us!

10.13.15.en: You are wonderful in Your justice as in Your love.

10.13.16.en: Reveal to me Your glory in the midst of my sufferings!
